global_caption: The video contains 7 shots and is a realistic, cool-toned action short of traditional Chinese dance in space. The overall color palette centers on icy blue and silver gray, with clear and controlled metallic textures of the space station. Lighting throughout relies primarily on cold natural light from viewports and equipment contour highlights.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, wide-angle overhead shot combined with slight push-in. Composition centers the transparent observation module, with a cold white hatch frame in the foreground and slowly drifting stars and distant nebulae in the background. Deep depth of field fully establishes the spatial environment. A boy stands before the viewport, wearing lightweight dance attire with traditional Chinese patterns, holding long water sleeves motionless. His hem flutters slightly in weak airflow. Cold starlight traces fine lines along the sleeve edges. Low hums from equipment above provide continuous ambient texture, while faint hatch alerts echo from afar. The camera slowly moves forward, as if approaching a ritual about to begin.
shot2: Shot 2 connects to the previous shot with a hard cut, transitioning from full-frame eye-level to lateral tracking along the corridor. Composition uses the corridor's linear perspective to guide the viewer forward. Foreground occasionally passes handrails and light strips; background maintains a long, stable spatial order. The boy transitions from stillness to motion, stepping forward along the metal corridor and quickly spinning, with the sleeve tip skimming the ground. Fabric drags out longer delayed arcs under low gravity. The camera performs smooth lateral movement with slight acceleration, emphasizing spatial displacement and the initiation of motion.
shot3: Shot 3 enters via action-matched edit from previous shot, close-up at eye-level with slight offset. Focus locks on upper body and hands. Foreground blurs a fluttering sleeve edge. Background features cold metallic walls and a narrow window allowing a beam of side light. Light cuts across the wrist and cheek, highlighting the tense moment of exertion. The boy sharply flicks his wrist, instantly whipping the long sleeve open like a silver ribbon. Fabric first tightens, then bursts outward, forming continuous ripples extending beyond the frame. The sleeve edge creates a clear motion blur due to speed.
shot4: Shot 4 naturally enters via sleeve-edge wipe transition from previous shot, medium shot from low angle. Composition places the circular structure of the zero-gravity training chamber above. Foreground includes floating training markers and suspension points. Background shows curved walls and cold white indicator lights. After entering the chamber, the boy leverages momentum to leap and flip, rising from the bottom of the frame upward. Both sleeves form a nearly complete circle around his body under centrifugal and zero-gravity forces. Hem and hair tips show slight lag. The camera pans upward along the arc with slight orbiting, precisely following the rotation direction, reinforcing traditional Chinese dance technique in zero gravity.
shot5: Shot 5 follows a hard cut from previous shot, switching to wide-angle overhead view. Frame looks vertically down from above the training chamber. Handrails, floor light strips, and distant viewport form radial leading lines. Foreground shows internal handrail structures; background reveals faint starfield. The boy uses handrails to perform rapid consecutive steps and spins, toes tapping repeatedly. His body quickly changes orientation around a central point. Long sleeves and hem flow in the same direction as the distant starfield, creating unified rotational flow. Action reaches peak speed in the entire sequence but remains clearly traceable. The camera performs short-distance rotating overhead shot with slight pull-out, making both character trajectory and spatial structure clearly visible.
shot6: Shot 6 transitions via quick fade-in/fade-out to shift emotion. Medium-close shot from low angle. Composition places the large viewport behind the subject, who is positioned slightly below center. Foreground has slightly blurred floating dust particles. Background features icy blue universe and white edge glow. Backlight sharply defines the boy’s silhouette. After a series of high-speed actions, he suddenly stops, arms extended and firmly held still. Sleeve continues to swing slowly due to inertia. At this moment, the cabin broadcast softly announces 'Position stable. ' The camera slowly pushes in, emphasizing the moment of transition from passion to control and stability.
shot7: Shot 7 continues from previous shot with a pull-out to conclude. Ultra-wide eye-level shot from outside the transparent dome, observing the interior of the space station. Composition wraps the dome’s curve around the subject. Foreground features cold-colored structural edges of the station exterior. Background shows deep icy blue universe and sparse star clusters. The figure inside appears small yet resolute. The boy gathers his sleeves into a centered pose, shifting from outward expression to inward focus. Both sleeves slowly lower and press close to the body. Previously fast-moving fabric finally comes to complete rest. Emotion descends from post-climax exuberance into vast, cold afterglow. The camera continuously pulls back and slightly ascends, ultimately framing his solitary figure facing the cosmos within the massive transparent dome.
